evidence_quotes.quote: Thyolo District, Southern Malawi, were trained in photography and ethics.
Eight women were selected as co-researchers for the photovoice
The sample of 44 photos selected by the co-researchers captures
management in their communities or within formal governance
The empty buckets at the back show she does not have enough water.
Waiting times at the borehole are a big issue.

country.comment: Conducted in rural communities served by Chimvu Health Centre and Thekerani Rural Hospital in Thyolo District, Southern Malawi.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 2.1

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative photovoice study with no quantitative effect estimates. Empirical findings center on physical, seasonal/climatic, infrastructural, and gendered household barriers to water access, quantity, quality, and reliability; exclusion from formal water governance is posited as framing context rather than empirically tested.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across 8 women co-researchers and 44 selected photographs in rural Thyolo District, 7 of 8 co-researchers reported having no water source in their village, documenting heavy maternal and newborn health/hygiene burdens from long walking distances, long borehole queues, seasonal droughts and river flooding, unfixed borehole breakdowns (prompting ad hoc collective village digging of makeshift wells), and household rationing between clean borehole water and contaminated unprotected sources; women's marginalization in community and formal water governance is noted as context, while participatory photovoice workshops (with 3 local leaders and community validation exhibitions) amplified women's voices for advocacy.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 3, Section 2.2.1; PDF pp. 4-10, Sections 3.1-3.3; PDF pp. 12-13, Section 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Women's exclusion from community and formal water governance structures is posited in the Abstract, Introduction (citing external literature), and Discussion as motivation rather than empirically observed operating on water access in the results; participatory photovoice served as the research/advocacy methodology and communal well-digging reflected informal village self-help when pumps broke down, so formal legal/administrative mechanisms are inferred only (0).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF pp. 4-10, Section 3; PDF pp. 12-13, Section 4

mechanism_flags.comment: None of the four top-level legal/administrative barrier families (ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT) are empirically studied; detailed code participation applies to the framing on women's exclusion from community and formal water governance decision-making, the participatory photovoice engagement with local leaders and community validation meetings, and communal self-help in digging a makeshift well when a borehole pump broke down.
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF pp. 2-4, Sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.4; PDF p. 9, Section 3.2; PDF pp. 12-13, Section 4

outcome_flags.comment: Co-researchers directly documented lack of village water points and long distances/queues (water_access), borehole breakdowns and seasonal dry spells/flooding blocking river crossing (service_reliability), insufficient water volumes forcing rationing (service_quantity), and biological/sediment contamination in unprotected rivers, streams, and wells vs protected boreholes (service_quality). Hygiene practices are extensively covered; sanitation facilities (latrines/sewerage) are not empirically analyzed in Results despite a passing mention of inadequate sanitation in the Abstract.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 4-10, Sections 3.1-3.3, Table 1, and Figures 1-10

publication_year.comment: Published 09 June 2025 in Frontiers in Global Women's Health.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, header metadata, citation block, and copyright statement

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary qualitative participatory photovoice study using group photo-elicitation discussions and phenomenological analysis; appraised with CASP Qualitative Checklist.

sample_size.comment: 3 local leaders (2 in Chimvu, 1 in Thekerani) also attended the workshops, and broader community members attended validation exhibitions (exact headcount of exhibition attendees not reported). Data collection took place February-May 2024.
sample_size.value: 8 women co-researchers (4 mothers and 4 guardians) across 2 rural health facility catchment communities (Chimvu and Thekerani); 44 selected photographs analyzed (21 from Chimvu out of 140 taken; 23 from Thekerani out of 141 taken)
